page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Notes in the right margin, from the top down to about the middle of the page. Full-width text continues below them to the foot.

main_text.p: NOn solet deterior condicio fieri eorum, qui li-tem v.l.58.s.de verb.obl.adde contestati sunt, quàm si non non essent sed ple-runque melior.
NEmo enim in persequendo deteriore causam, sed meliorem facit. Denique post litem contestatam heredi d.l.58. quoque prospiceretur, & heres l.52.s.de rei vindicat. te-netur ex omnibus causis.
NVlla intelligitur mora ibi fieri, vbi cap.non est in mora 60.de reg.in 6: l.40. nulla pe-titio est f.s.de vcb. cred.l.27.s.de verb.oblig: 2..
QVamdiu possit valere testamentum, tamdiu le-gitimus Eclog.3. cap. 86: l.54.s.de pactis. & ita intellige l.4. non admittitur Cod. de con.-prasum..
IN omnibus f multo mi- quidem, maxime tamen in iure (k, l) quitas [?] spectanda sit.
QVotiens duplici [?] iure defertur [?] alicui [?] suc-cessio: repudiato nouo [?] iure, quod ante defer-nus poena, quia non debetur poena sine mora. [?]
{e} cap.non est in mora 60.de reg.in 6: l.40.

page.notes: Scan is faded and the marginal references are partly illegible; several note markers (k, l, m, n, o, p, q) and the text of the lower notes are read tentatively and need checking against the original. The Greek-style and abbreviated references (e.g. "Hotom.", "vulgat. Hal.") are as printed. The bottom lines of the page (continuation of 91, with notes "accuir. heredi", "h nisi voluntas testatoris obstet", "i demus enim iuris solemnibus aliquid deesse?" etc.) are dense and only partly legible; they are not fully transcribed here and need a second pass on a higher-resolution scan.
